Container.Name: NextDash
Container.DonateText: Find NextDash useful? Consider supporting the project.
Container.Overview:
NextDash is a lightweight, self-hosted bookmark dashboard that features a minimalist, keyboard-driven interface with extensive customization options, making it the perfect personal dashboard for power users. Based on the excellent ThinkDashboard.
Key features: • Keyboard-driven navigation for fast access to all your bookmarks • Extensive theme and layout customization, with a theme studio beside the dashboard and a theme editor • Inbox to collect new links fast: triage them, or keep them under Bookmarks → Unsorted and file whole groups later • Bookmarks view with Health built in: finds broken, stale and duplicate links, with uptime monitoring and downtime alerts • Edit mode: change categories, widgets and pages right on the dashboard • A checkup and a weekly digest that tell you what needs attention • Video bookmarks marked in the list, and played in the hover card without leaving the dashboard • Widgets beside your bookmarks: 48 built-in kinds (uptime, feeds, weather, calendar, disks, containers and more) plus a Custom widget for any JSON API • Your media stack on the dashboard: Jellyfin, Sonarr, Radarr, Seerr, qBittorrent and SABnzbd, with the posters from your own library • Finds the web apps in your Docker containers and offers them as bookmarks, with an icon and a status check (needs the Docker socket below) • Glances on the dashboard: a page for the hosts you run Glances on, with processes, containers, graphs and incidents, and a widget for one host • Your Unraid server on the dashboard: seven widgets for the array, parity, shares, VMs, the UPS and notifications, with alerts • Web search in the search panel through your own SearXNG or the Brave Search API • Six interface languages: English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish and Chinese • Lightweight and fast, no heavy dependencies • Actively maintained with regular releases
Links: • Website: https://www.nextdash.cc • Source code and releases: https://github.com/jordibrouwer/nextdash • Changelog: https://github.com/jordibrouwer/nextdash/releases • Devlog / release updates: https://www.nextdash.cc/news • Also available on GHCR: ghcr.io/jordibrouwer/nextdash:latest • User manual: https://github.com/jordibrouwer/nextdash/blob/main/MANUAL.md
The host widgets (Processor, Memory, Disks, Containers) are off until you fill in the optional paths and variables below — they are hidden under Show more settings. Section 15.4 of the manual explains what each one reads.
Support: open an issue on GitHub via the Support link above. Bug reports and feature requests are welcome.

### v1.22.5 (2026-10-29) - Recent bookmarks: * shows tiles with the day you opened them, from every page, ten at a time - Tag view: show bookmarks with any tag or with every tag, put a tag on ticked rows with Add tag, and sort by score - Action bar: a theme studio button, and a docked bar comes back when you rest the pointer on its edge - Dashboard: every window opens in the middle, and the page filter (Shift+F) takes several words - Edit mode: the panel says what is in a block and offers its actions - Glances: the Hosts table puts hosts in trouble first, sorts, names the fullest disk's mount and draws the processor's last hour - Appearance: Ocean is the theme a new install starts on - Fixes: a setting changed on another device survives closing the theme studio, and a right-click menu stays open in edit mode
### v1.22.4 (2026-10-29) - Edit mode: Shift+M or the pencil in the action bar edits names, icons, widths, views and a widget's settings in a panel beside the page - Search: a Usually now group in the empty panel, and the right arrow on a result unfolds open, edit, copy and move - Checkup: :checkup walks through dead links, duplicates, bookmarks never opened, empty pages and widgets that show an error - Weekly digest: it opens on an Overview with the week in figures, and says since when a link is down and why - Widgets: adding one is a guided step that tests the address or key first - Config: Finders is a section of its own - Fixes: the demo server starts faster, icons the outbound limit refused are fetched again, and a page of uncategorised bookmarks no longer counts as empty
### v1.22.3 (2026-10-28) - First start: the Quick start asks whether to keep the example links, offers ready-made pages (Homelab, Media server, Developer) and a CSV import, and lists ten steps - Tours and tips: a keyboard tour, tours for Config Monitoring and Unraid, tips that can come weekly, and a settings search that remembers what you opened - Offers: check images for updates, re-check old links, the browser extension and what changed after an update, each with its own switch - Appearance: the docked action bar and the command palette take more of your theme, and Config's title stays clear of its buttons - Privacy: the analytics send an install code and a hostname replaced by one word, and send less often - Security: golang.org/x/net v0.62.0
### v1.22.2 (2026-10-26) - Appearance: the action bar, the Bookmarks, Inbox, Containers, Glances, Tags and Config views are drawn like a category in every material, and the blocks in Config lie on their pane as a tint
### v1.22.1 (2026-10-26) - Dashboard: a click on a bookmark icon opens the bookmark - Weekly digest: a clearer window and :digest, plus an overview panel - Health: an Uptime badge section with Copy Markdown and Copy HTML - Widgets: Retry all on the Feeds widget - Fixes: a Glances 5 server is no longer called version 3, and the key legend sits inside its panel
### v1.22.0 (2026-10-25) - Appearance: every theme is redrawn with a surface of its own for each material, Aurora Glass is the default and every install moved onto it once, with a way back - Backdrops: 75 of them, a pool for each material, and a Quiet centre slider that fades the backdrop behind your bookmarks - Appearance: Material style (Signature or Classic), the neutral themes share one accent, and ThinkDashboard Classic is back - Keyboard: a cheat sheet you can search, and Shift+G opens Glances from every view - Bookmarks: the add and edit form has two columns with a live preview of the card - Config: Overview lists the new features since v1.20.3, and its manual link goes to nextdash.cc/docs - Fixes: Export CSV and the imports work before Data & backups is opened, Home and End work on tabs and charts, and a focused block title shows its focus

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the NextDash web interface

Config.Name: AppData
Config.Description: Persistent storage path for NextDash data (bookmarks, settings)

Config.Name: Write token
Config.Description: Optional. Require this token in the X-NextDash-Token header on every write. Leave empty for an open instance on a trusted network.

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: Optional. Addresses and CIDR ranges whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed, comma-separated — set this if nextDash sits behind a reverse proxy, so rate limits count per visitor instead of per proxy. Left empty the header is ignored.

Config.Name: Allowed hosts
Config.Description: Optional. Only with a write token: public host names the dashboard may be opened by, comma-separated (*.example.com allowed, * turns the check off). IP addresses, localhost and private names (.local, .lan) always work. Needed when you open nextDash by your own domain.

Config.Name: Host proc
Config.Description: Optional. Mount the host /proc here for the Processor and Memory widgets. Host path: /proc

Config.Name: Host proc variable
Config.Description: Optional. Set to /host/proc once the mount above is filled in.

Config.Name: Host disks
Config.Description: Optional. Mount the array here for the Disks widget. Host path: /mnt — then name /mnt/user or /mnt/cache in the widget.

Config.Name: Host root variable
Config.Description: Optional. Set to /host/root once the disks mount above is filled in.

Config.Name: Docker socket
Config.Description: Optional. Mount the Docker socket here for the Containers widget. Host path: /var/run/docker.sock — read-only still exposes the daemon's whole read API, so use a socket proxy if that is too much.

Config.Name: Docker socket variable
Config.Description: Optional. Set to /var/run/docker.sock once the socket mount above is filled in. Unset, the Containers widget is hidden.

Config.Name: Docker actions
Config.Description: Optional. 1 lets the Containers view start, stop, update and remove containers; 0 keeps it read-only. A writable socket is root on the host, so set a write token as well.

Config.Name: Run as root
Config.Description: Optional. 1 keeps nextDash running as root, needed only when the Docker socket belongs to root's group (gid 0). Unraid's socket belongs to the docker group (gid 281), so leave this at 0 here.
